MAJOR NEW FINDING: a reproducible, severe degenerate-repetition-loop bug. Two of eight questions (Q1 XM30, Q8 SPECTRO ISR) produced a genuinely good, well-structured, properly-cited opening (direct answer + key facts with real inline [n] citations + analyst assessment), then entered an infinite loop inside the '## פערים / מה לא ידוע' (gaps) section, repeating a small set of near-identical bullet points verbatim (in Q1's case, combinatorially growing hyphenated compound words like 'המלחמה הפוליטית-חברתית-כלכלית-...') for 500+ seconds and 30,000-49,000+ characters without ever reaching the sources sentinel or a natural stop. This was not an artifact of my own tooling: the pattern is identical in both independent occurrences and the growth is clearly a decoding degeneracy in the 'gaps' section specifically, not a network issue. This is a materially worse failure mode than a clean timeout (round 0's chat questions mostly returned nothing at all within 120s) because it burns GPU time and produces user-visible garbage rather than nothing.

Completion, this round (300s wall-clock enforced, one retry after ~2min on timeout, per protocol): Q2, Q3, Q4, Q6 (after 1 retry), Q7 completed cleanly and quickly (25-42s each). Q5 timed out at 300s with partial content, and confirmed as a true timeout on retry (30s read-gap, zero bytes -- GPU busy). Q1 and Q8 hit the repetition-loop describe above and were not force-retried (the failure mode was already conclusively identified from the first run in each case).

Only Q1 (before it looped) and Q8 (before it looped) showed correct [n] usage tied to real content.

Hallucination/conflation rate remains very high across the substantive answers: Q2 (Iron Beam) answers almost entirely about a Rafael-India 'Iron Dome (Tamir)' manufacturing deal while mislabeling it 'Iron Beam (Tamir)' -- Tamir is Iron Dome's interceptor, Iron Beam is a laser system with no interceptor at all, a real system-conflation error. Q3 (Greece LORA) never once discusses LORA (an IAI precision-strike missile) and instead answers entirely about Greece's unrelated $3.5-4B David's Sling/Barak-MX/Spyder air-defense package -- the two LORA citations actually retrieved are about Germany, not Greece, and the model silently substitutes topics rather than flagging the gap; also highly repetitive across its own sections, unchanged from round 0's complaint about this exact question. Q4 (DROIC trend) and Q7 (latest US EO/IR RFI) both cite and describe the SAME unrelated academic arXiv paper ('Residual Optimal Transport-Based Experts Collaboration...', item 127, a visible/infrared object-DETECTION paper) as if it were, respectively, the leading DROIC HARDWARE technology and a government RFI document -- neither framing is defensible, and the repeated appearance of this one paper across two different unrelated questions suggests a retrieval/embedding pollution issue rather than two independent judgment errors. Q6 (AUSA 2026) produced a generic, plausible-sounding answer entirely ungrounded in its own retrieved citations (none of which are actually about AUSA). Q5's partial transcript (before its timeout) shows probable category errors comparing Barak-8 (a naval air-defense system) and Arrow-3 (an exo-atmospheric interceptor) as if they were C-UAS systems comparable to Skyranger.

Net assessment vs round 0: a modest completion-rate improvement and the markdown-rendering fix are real, but they are offset by a severe newly-discovered repetition-loop failure mode and an unchanged-to-worse hallucination/conflation rate on the answers that do complete.
